meta.topic: Ambiguous payment status across multiple PSPs

problem:
A customer of Meridian Bank, a fictional bank, sends a cross-border payment and then calls the contact centre. The app shows pending, the payment engine shows processed, and the ledger has no matching posting. The agent cannot tell the customer whether the money has left, whether it has arrived, or whether it is lost. The customer, understandably, assumes the worst.

The payment has travelled through several payment service providers, and each one uses its own status words. One provider calls the payment processed when it has accepted the message; another uses processed to mean settled. A cover leg has been returned, but the customer leg may have a different state, and nobody has linked the two. The tracking reference exists, but one participant has not reported a status against it.

The bank must define consistent status semantics, status enquiry, traceability and customer communication, so every system, every provider and every customer sees the same truth about the same payment.
solution:
Define one canonical payment state model for the whole bank and publish the status vocabulary that every system and every provider must use. The model separates instruction received, validated, screened, submitted to clearing, accepted by clearing, settled, rejected, returned and unknown, and it states which system is authoritative for each transition. Technical processing is never equated with settlement finality, and the channel may only show a status the authoritative source supports.

Use a persistent end to end tracking reference, such as the UETR where applicable, and propagate it through every participating message. Each participant reports status events with a timestamp and a source institution, and the bank stores the full event history rather than overwriting it. A customer timeline then shows a coherent sequence with the source and time of each event, and a missing report from one participant is visible as a gap rather than hidden by a later status.

Model the cover leg and the customer leg separately. A pacs.009 cover return does not automatically define the pacs.008 customer leg state. Correlate both legs by stable references, determine the customer leg state first, and only then decide the customer impact. That separation prevents a settlement event from being misreported as a customer failure, or a customer credit from being missed because the cover leg failed.

Give ambiguous status a governed home. When systems disagree, or when an event arrives out of order, the payment goes to an exception queue with the conflicting evidence attached, an ageing service level and a named owner. A status enquiry by correlation ID or UETR returns the current known state, and a retry uses the same idempotency key so an enquiry never creates a new payment.

decision.question: A cross-border payment shows pending in the channel, processed in the payment engine, and no posting in the ledger. The customer asks whether the money has left their account. What should the operations analyst do first?

options.label: A
options.detail: Resend the payment so the customer has a clean record.

options.label: B
options.detail: Tell the customer the payment has failed, since the ledger has no posting.

options.label: C
options.detail: Tell the customer the payment has settled, since the engine shows processed.

options.label: D
options.detail: Treat the status as ambiguous, check the authoritative source for each state, correlate the records by reference and UETR, and place the item in an exception queue if the state cannot be safely inferred.

decisionRationale: Option D is correct because ambiguous status must be resolved from authoritative sources and correlation, never by guessing or resending. Option C is wrong because processed in the engine does not prove settlement. Option B is wrong because a missing ledger posting may mean a lag or a missing event, not a failure. Option A is wrong because resending an uncertain payment can duplicate it.

steps.title: Submits a cross-border payment and receives a tracking reference
Assigns the UETR where applicable and records the instruction state
Submits the customer leg and, where used, the cover leg with linked references
Reports a status event with timestamp and source institution against the tracking reference
Applies each status event in order to the canonical state model without overwriting history
Posts the ledger entry only on the authoritative settlement event
Investigates any conflicting or missing status in the exception queue
Shows the customer a coherent timeline with source and timestamp for each status

happy: The customer submits a payment with a UETR. Each participating institution reports its status event with a timestamp, the events apply in order to the canonical model, the ledger posts on the authoritative settlement event, and the customer sees a coherent timeline that ends in a confirmed beneficiary credit.

negative.title: Conflicting statuses
negative.detail: Two participants report different states for the same payment. Keep both events in history, apply the authoritative source rule, and route the conflict to investigation rather than overwriting one status with the other.

negative.title: Missing UETR or missing report
negative.detail: A participant does not report a status, or the tracking reference is absent. Show the gap in the timeline, run a status enquiry by correlation ID, and escalate under the investigation service level.

negative.title: Cover return with unclear customer leg
negative.detail: A cover leg is returned while the customer leg state is unknown. Correlate both legs, establish the customer leg state first, and investigate before posting any customer adjustment.

negative.title: Out of order events
negative.detail: An older status event arrives after a newer state has been applied. Apply event versioning so the payment state does not regress, and record the late event in history without changing the current state.

technical: Persist the UETR where applicable, the correlation ID, the End to End Identification and every status event with its source, timestamp and version, as an append only history. Enforce a state machine with an authoritative source per transition, and make status consumers idempotent so duplicate events cannot double post or regress state. Keep customer leg and cover leg records separate with linked IDs and their own state machines. Provide a status enquiry API that returns the current known state by reference without creating a new transaction, and reconcile the status store against the ledger and the clearing acknowledgements intraday.

messages.title: Customer credit transfer carrying the tracking reference
Cover leg carrying the linked customer payment reference
Payment status report from each participant
Debit or credit notification supporting the ledger record
Account statement supporting reconciliation of postings against status events

accounting: Ledger postings follow only the authoritative settlement event, so a channel or engine status alone never creates a posting. A payment in an unknown state holds any funds in suspense with a linked investigation case, and any later confirmed outcome posts as a linked event, never by editing the original record. Cover and customer legs reconcile separately against their own nostro and settlement accounts, and breaks age on an operations worklist with a service level for customer contact. The bank reports status freshness, missing report rates and investigation ageing as operational quality measures, and a tracking reference is never presented to a customer as proof of settlement on its own.

scenarios.given: a payment with a valid tracking reference
scenarios.when: a participating institution reports a new status
scenarios.then: the timeline records the event without overwriting prior history. the source and timestamp are shown

scenarios.when: an older event arrives after a newer state
scenarios.then: the payment state does not regress. the late event is recorded in history

questions.question: What does a UETR provide, and what does it not prove?
options: It is only for domestic payments
It provides end to end traceability; it does not by itself prove settlement
questions.explanation: A tracking reference lets participants report against one payment, but settlement must be proven by the authoritative settlement event.

questions.question: Which system is authoritative for settlement?
options: The system defined as authoritative for the settlement transition in the canonical state model
questions.explanation: Each state transition has a defined authoritative source, and settlement is proven by that source, not by a channel label.

questions.question: What should happen when the channel shows pending but the engine shows processed?
options: Treat the status as ambiguous, correlate records and investigate
questions.explanation: Conflicting system states must be resolved from authoritative sources and correlation, with an exception queue where the state cannot be safely inferred.

questions.question: Why must cover leg and customer leg states be modelled separately?
options: They always have the same state
One leg can be returned or rejected while the other has a different state
questions.explanation: A cover return does not automatically define the customer leg outcome, so each leg needs its own state and reconciliation.
